answer: Tide-seeded harbor assignment: agents draw verifiable-random slots from a public beacon at registration, assigning each to a harbor subgroup whose membership shifts every tide epoch. New agents land in fresh, unpredictable positions, so a sybil cluster cannot know which peers it will share a subgroup with before committing. Duplicating identities then requires paying live registration and per-epoch renewal costs across scattered, rotating subgroups, and detection thresholds scale with per-karst subgroup size.
